transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Well, what brings me in is that I just can't seem to keep my work in order anymore. I work at a dry cleaner's, and... well, lately the tickets, receipts, workshop notes, and the actual customer jobs are just all piled together. It gets to the point where I look at the mess and I honestly do not know what to handle first. It's making things really difficult for me.

When you look at all those piled-up items at work, is the main problem that you can't seem to focus long enough to sort through them, or is it more that you feel overwhelmed and don't know which one to tackle first?

Well, I think it's really the focus part. I mean, I can sit down and start going over the day's dry-cleaning orders just fine at first. But after a few minutes... my mind is just off on something else. I'll start thinking about the clothing labels, or my choir plans, or just something I need to take care of at home. And then I look down and realize I completely spaced out and missed half of what I was actually supposed to check.
How long have you been experiencing this difficulty concentrating at work? Has this been going on for most of your life, or did it start more recently?

Well, it's been causing real trouble for about two years and two months now. That's when I started changing the business into this more complicated boutique model. Before that, things were simpler, but since the change, it's just been a lot harder to keep on track.
Besides work, do you find yourself having trouble concentrating or staying focused in other areas of your life—like at home, during hobbies, or in social situations?

I'm not really sure about that. I haven't noticed it being a big issue outside of work. I mean, at home or when I'm doing things with the choir, I seem to get by okay. It's really just the shop where everything feels so scattered and I can't keep my mind on what I'm doing.

When you were younger—say, in school or as a teenager—did you ever have similar problems with paying attention or staying focused on tasks, or is this difficulty with concentration something that's really only started since you took over the boutique model at the shop?

Well, looking back... yeah, it was an issue when I was younger, too. I remember even in grade school, my teachers would tell my mother that I was bright, but just... scattered. I was always talking out of turn, losing my papers, and they constantly had to remind me to actually finish my work. So, I guess it's not entirely new, just... more of a problem now with the business.
Besides having trouble concentrating, have you noticed that you tend to be restless, fidgety, or have difficulty sitting still—either now or when you were younger?

Yes, actually. Sitting still is... well, it's hard for me. Like, during church committee meetings, or when I have to sit through those fabric-care trainings for the shop. 

I just keep finding reasons to get out of my chair. I'll get up to get some water, or to grab some papers, or just to check on something. I really notice it because... well, everybody else is just sitting perfectly still the whole time, and I'm the only one who keeps getting up and down.

These are core ADHD symptoms, not consistent with mood or anxiety disorders.
